statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive and do not support or define the Jacobian vector product (the source wikipedia:Jacobian_matrix_and_determinant defines only the Jacobian matrix and its determinant, containing no derivation or mention of a Jacobian vector product). By definition, for a differentiable vector-valued function f: R^n -> R^m at a point x in R^n and a vector v in R^n, the Jacobian-vector product (JVP) is the product of the Jacobian matrix J_f(x) and the vector v, given by (J_f(x)) v = sum_{j=1}^n (df/dx_j) v_j, where the Jacobian matrix is the m x n matrix of all first-order partial derivatives [df_i/dx_j].

symbols.meaning: Jacobian matrix of first-order partial derivatives
vector by which the Jacobian matrix is multiplied

properties.property: The Jacobian matrix is the matrix of all first-order partial derivatives of a vector-valued function of several variables, generalizing the derivative and differential.
properties.why: each entry (i, j) is defined as the partial derivative of component f_i with respect to variable x_j

properties.property: According to the inverse function theorem, the matrix inverse of the Jacobian matrix of an invertible function is the Jacobian matrix of the inverse function: J_{f^{-1}}(p) = J_f^{-1}(f^{-1}(p)).
properties.why: f is locally invertible near points where the Jacobian is continuous and nonsingular

properties.property: At a critical point of a differentiable function, the rank of the Jacobian matrix is strictly lower than maximal, meaning all minors of maximal rank are zero.
properties.why: the dimension of the differential image drops below its maximal possible value

assumptions.assumption: The vector-valued function f must be differentiable at point x, meaning all first-order partial derivatives exist.
assumptions.breaks_when: One or more partial derivatives df_i/dx_j do not exist or are undefined at x.

assumptions.assumption: The vector v must have dimension matching the number of input variables n of the function f.
assumptions.breaks_when: The dimension of vector v differs from the column dimension n of the Jacobian matrix.

failure_modes.signature: Entries of the Jacobian matrix evaluate to undefined, NaN, or infinity
failure_modes.cause: Function components fail to be differentiable at the evaluation point x.

failure_modes.signature: Matrix-vector multiplication J_f(x) v is undefined
failure_modes.cause: The vector v has length different from the input dimension n of f.

failure_modes.signature: The rank of the Jacobian matrix is not maximal (det(J_f) = 0 for square systems)
failure_modes.cause: Linear dependence among rows or columns of partial derivatives at x.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so jacobian_vector_product is recorded as a definition
